tactics.name: Impersonating a trusted authority
tactics.summary: The caller claims to be your bank, a well-known company, or the police. The name does the work before a single fact is checked.
tactics.spot_it: A caller's claimed identity is not evidence of it. Hang up and dial the number printed on your card, your bill, or the official website - never a number the caller gives you.

tactics.name: Manufactured urgency
tactics.summary: A deadline that exists only inside the call. Your account closes, the fine doubles, the offer expires - all so you act before you verify.
tactics.spot_it: Real institutions let you call back. If someone insists this cannot wait, that pressure is the product, not a detail.

tactics.name: Manufactured fear
tactics.summary: A fake virus warning, a breached account, a legal threat. Panic is easier to steer than curiosity.
tactics.spot_it: Notice the feeling before the content. Being frightened into a fast decision is itself the warning sign.

tactics.name: The impossible scan
tactics.summary: A web page announcing it has scanned your computer and found infections. A page in a browser cannot inspect your machine, so the result was written before you arrived.
tactics.spot_it: Any site claiming to have scanned your device is lying about something it is physically unable to do.

tactics.name: Talking you into handing over the controls
tactics.summary: Posing as technical support to get you to install remote-access software, which hands over your screen, your files and your accounts at once.
tactics.spot_it: Nobody legitimate cold-calls to ask for remote access. If you did not start the support request, there is no support request.

tactics.name: A fee to fix an invented problem
tactics.summary: Payment for repairing something that was never broken - the problem, the diagnosis and the cure all supplied by the same stranger.
tactics.spot_it: Whoever reports the problem should never be the one charging to solve it. Get a second opinion from someone who called nobody.

tactics.name: The same call, more than once
tactics.summary: The identical wording turning up at a neighbour, a relative, a community group. Scripts are reused because they are cheap and they work.
tactics.spot_it: Compare notes out loud. A call that felt uniquely targeted usually turns out to have reached half the street.

tactics.name: The reused victim list
tactics.summary: Names and numbers are traded and worked repeatedly. Answering once, even to refuse, confirms a real person is on the end of the line.
tactics.spot_it: Being called again is not bad luck. If the calls keep coming, treat the number as known and let unknown callers go to voicemail.

tactics.name: Denying you time to check
tactics.summary: Different scripts, one shared mechanism: keep the person on the line and away from anyone who could confirm the story.
tactics.spot_it: The single defence that works on every version of this - end the call and check independently. Any caller who resists that has told you what they are.
